[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
Matthew Glasgow was born before 1542, probably in Scotland. The year is an estimate based on his being at least 18 years old when he appeared as a tenant in a record dated 1559–60.

In the Cunninghame teind lists of 1559–60, Matthew Glasgow and John Mathie were listed under Ardeer Nether in the parish of Stevenston, Ayrshire.<ref>Margaret H. B. Sanderson, ''The People of Sixteenth Century Ayrshire'', ''Ayrshire Collections'', vol. 14, no. 8 (Ayrshire Archaeological and Natural History Society, 1987), appendix "The Cunninghame Teind Lists of 1559–60," [https://aanhs.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/people-of-ayrshire.pdf#page=36 p. 331], Ardeer Nether entry. Sanderson identifies the underlying record as Scottish Record Office, Register of Acts and Decreets, vol. 22, fols. 102v–167v.</ref> Sanderson explains that those named were tenants responsible for crop teinds and that the list does not necessarily identify the holding on which a family lived.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1168]] is assessed at 46% (possible). No parent is named. James elder of Corsankell is selected as a possible father or uncle of Matthew at Ardeer Nether from their common 1559–60 Stevenston tenant cluster and compatible generations. The same Stevenston estate landscape and an ordinary generation make James elder the preferred local father candidate, although nephew is also a natural fit.

Possible father, not a statement that the teind list names Matthew as James’s son. The proved James and John sons do not exclude another child.

Next useful test: Look for a succession, tenancy or kin clause linking Matthew with Corsankell.

Source basis already held: [https://aanhs.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/people-of-ayrshire.pdf#page=36 Margaret H. B. Sanderson, The People of Sixteenth Century Ayrshire, appendix “The Cunninghame Teind Lists of 1559-60,” p. 331 (https://aanhs.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/people-of-ayrshire.pdf#page=36).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.

=

* Birth: before 1542, Scotland, uncertain.
* Death: after 1558, place unknown, uncertain.

No reviewed source identifies Matthew's parents, spouse, children, precise birthplace, residence, or death. Ardeer Nether should therefore not be entered as his birth or death place.

=== Wider Mathie–Glencairn connection ===

The Ardeer pairing belongs to a wider documented association. On 10 May 1554 David Mathy and [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]] were named together among the Glasgow burgesses witnessing the same sasines.<ref name="Mathie1554">Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 1, protocols 183–184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n90/mode/2up 10 May 1554, printed p. 63].</ref> David had a recorded son John. A John Mathie was admitted as a burgess with James, Earl of Glencairn, James Cunningham and the earl’s servant William Cochrane in 1583.<ref name="MathieGlencairn">James R. Anderson, ed., Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750 (Scottish Record Society, 1925), [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso43scotuoft.pdf entry for 8 February 1582/83].</ref>

Tutory retours entered on 20 January 1607 identify the deceased John Mathie of Ibert’s full brother as Matthew Mathie, burgess of Glasgow, and name John’s lawful children James, David, Agnes and Margaret.<ref name="Ibert1607">Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum ... Abbreviatio, vol. 2, tutory retours 100–101, 20 January 1607, [https://books.google.com/books?id=PiVDAAAAcAAJ digitised volume]; underlying register, National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browsetreeview.aspx?reference=C22 C22/3].</ref> Ibert lay in Kilmaronock within the Glencairn estate network. This gives the Mathie household a direct link back to Glasgow burgh society, although it does not identify [[Glasgow-3908|Matthew Glasgow]] as a relative.

[[Mathie-159|Jonet Mathie]] married [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] in Glasgow on 25 January 1618.<ref name="Mathie1618">FamilySearch, “Scotland Marriages, 1561–1910,” John Glasgow and Jonet Mathie, 25 January 1618, Glasgow, Lanark, Scotland; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYWK-WM3 permanent record].</ref> Her marriage may continue this association between the families.

This Matthew is not [[Glasgow-3538|Matthew Glasgow]], who was named at Pyperheugh in the same parish in 1665. No evidence currently establishes a relationship between the two men.

=== Possible family placement ===
[[Glasgow-1168|James Glasgow elder of Corsankell]] is Matthew's leading possible father or uncle. Matthew at Ardeer Nether and James elder at Corsankell were separately named as tenant or householder figures in the same 1559-60 Stevenston teind list.<ref>Margaret H. B. Sanderson, ''The People of Sixteenth Century Ayrshire'', appendix “The Cunninghame Teind Lists of 1559-60,” [https://aanhs.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/people-of-ayrshire.pdf#page=36 p. 331].</ref> A 1571 writ expressly names James elder's sons James and John, but does not purport to list every child.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Charter Chest of the Earls of Glencairn, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD39%2F5%2F59 GD39/5/59], 9 February 1571.</ref>

The locality and generation make Matthew a possible son, nephew or younger collateral, but no record states the relationship. James is therefore attached only as an uncertain working father. [[Glasgow-3911|Michael Glasgow]] is a distinct man and is better treated as an older collateral in the same estate network.
